verses.1: And the serpent of Amnon rose up and sat on Jebus. All the people of Jebus said to him, “We have made a covenant with you; we will serve you.”
verses.2: And the serpent said to them, “This will be a sign for you: every eye that looks at this will be filled with shame and disgrace for all of Israel.”
verses.3: And they said to him, “The elders of Jabesh Gilead will give us seven days. Then the devils will be sent out into all the borders of Israel. If there is no one who can save us, then we will go to you.”
verses.4: And the magicians came to Sheol. They spoke those words into the ears of the people. All the people raised their voices and cried out in joy.
verses.5: And behold, Shaul came in the afternoon from the field. He said, “What shall I do with this people? Should they offer sacrifices?” Then they told him what the people of Yevi had said.
verses.6: And the Spirit of God fell upon Shaul when he heard these words. He was filled with joy.
verses.7: And he took a dove in the morning, and released it. He sent it throughout all the borders of Israel, through the hands of the magicians, with the command: “No one should come after Shaul or Shemuel.” So that would be what would happen to the dove. Fear of the Lord fell upon the people. They left, like one person.
verses.8: And they were scattered throughout the land. So, there were three hundred thousand Israelites, and thirty thousand Judaeans.
verses.9: And they said to the magicians who came: “Tell a man from Gilad that there will be no more darkness for you after this. Just like the sun never goes down.” Then the magicians came and told the people of Gilad. They were very happy.
verses.10: And they said, “After tomorrow, the people of Yavish will come to you. They will do everything good for us, as you desire.”
verses.11: In the evening, Shemuel divided the people into three groups. They entered the camp in accordance with the rules of the day. They fought against their enemies until the end of the day. The remaining people fled, and only two of them remained alive.
verses.12: And the people said to Samuel, “Who is this man who says that Shaul will be our king? Let them be killed!”
verses.13: And Shaul said, “No one will be able to do anything on this day, for today is a day when Jehovah has brought salvation to Israel.”
verses.14: And Shemuel said to the people, “Go, and let us go down into the valley. There, we will establish a kingdom.”
verses.15: And all the people of Gilgal went there. They made Shaul king over them in place of Jehovah. They offered sacrifices to Jehovah. Shaul and all the people of Israel celebrated there for many days.
